lots.what_it_is: Zip bag of circulated Australian silver sixpences, mostly George VI (one coin reads 1942 with a D mint mark), title weight 64.3 g. At 2.82 g per sixpence that is about 22 to 23 coins. Dates of most coins are not legible, so the split between .925 (to 1945) and .500 (1946 onwards) coins is unknown.
lots.guide_summary: No SOLD, UNSOLD or ASKING evidence survives (the researcher returned none and the WebSearch budget is exhausted, also refused when I tried). Value rests on silver melt only, which is my arithmetic, not a price paid: kitco spot bid USD 61.06/oz (page opened 1 Oct 2026) x 1.438252 (open.er-api.com, 1 Oct 2026) = AUD 87.82/oz = AUD 2.82/g. If all 64.3 g is .925: 64.3 x 0.925 x 2.82 = about AUD 168. If half the coins are .500: about AUD 130. Dealers usually buy junk silver below melt, so realistic resale is roughly AUD 110 to 160.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so both maximum bids are 0 under the rules. For reference only: melt AUD 130 to 168. If bidding on melt alone, an all-in cost below melt means hammer below 130/1.198 = about AUD 108 (worst case .500 mix) or 168/1.198 = about AUD 140 (all sterling). This is not a SOLD-backed maximum.
lots.confidence_reason: No market entries at all; only a melt calculation. Dates and silver content not readable in the single photo.
lots.dropped_entries: None to drop (researcher returned no entries). Researcher's spot figure USD 60.63/oz was rechecked; kitco now shows USD 61.06/oz, which barely changes the melt.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo. About 22 to 30 sixpences visible loose in a bag, George VI obverses and Arms reverses, one date reads 1942 D. Handwritten sticker reads roughly '20.52 x' over '80' with a lot number scrawled over it, possibly a previous owner's or Gowans' estimate note, not legible enough to rely on.
lots.condition: Circulated, grey, worn. No key dates visible.
lots.question_for_gowans: How many coins are in the bag, and what date range? Are any dated 1946 or later (half silver) or any pre-1938 George V? Is 64.3 g the coins only or including the bag?

My read of the holders: 1938, 1940, 1941, 1942, 1942D, 1942S, 1943D, 1943S, 1944S, 1945, 1946, 1948, 1950, 1951, 1951PL, 1952. The researcher missed 1942S and 1943D and listed a plain 1943 that is not there. 11 are .925 silver (to 1945), 5 are .500 (1946 onwards). No major key date.

lots.guide_summary: All surviving evidence is ASKING (dealer retail for single Uncirculated coins), 0 sold, 0 unsold. Close entries run AUD 40 to 139 per coin in Unc; the lot's coins are mostly VF to EF and would retail well below that. Melt floor (my arithmetic, spot AUD 2.82/g): 11 x 2.82 g x 0.925 + 5 x 2.82 g x 0.5 = 35.8 g fine silver = about AUD 100. Range shown is per-coin Unc asking, not a lot value.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so both maximum bids are 0. Reference only: melt about AUD 100 (100/1.198 = about AUD 83 hammer for melt parity). Circulated singles of these dates typically trade at a fraction of Unc retail, so a lot value of perhaps AUD 120 to 250 is plausible but unverified.
lots.confidence_reason: Dates read clearly from the holders, but grades unknown and only asking evidence exists; no sold results could be searched (WebSearch budget exhausted).

lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm all 16 coins are present with the dates as pencilled, and whether the 1951 PL and 1950 'AU' coins have any cleaning or marks? Any noticeably uncirculated pieces?
